r3_note: Lesson is almost entirely the خرب / خرّب pair (past, present, command, feminine, plural, food sense) plus the N-verb recap at the end. Many of his Arabic lines between 18:14 and 36:00 are untranscribed ([speaking Arabic]), so A11, A12, A16 and D2 rest on Amal's recasts and his own English asides. Her 25:57 line also came out as 'rose راح يخرب' (engine dropped her el- too), which is why D6 is dropped. rows.medi_said: Review. What was the word for review? ... What is the word for review?
rows.amal_said: As a noun it's مراجعة. So what's-- what is it as a verb? ... صح، براجع.
rows.why: Didn't-know: he asked twice for the word for review (02:21, 02:32); she gave the noun مراجعة, asked for the verb, said صح to his مراجعة and supplied براجع herself - one supplied word, not a wrong form (sheet: review | Muraaja3a | مراجعة; i review | Ana baraaje3 | أنا براجع).
rows.r3_why: Same moment as r2's row; the transcript supports tier 0 (asked), not tier 2: he never produced a wrong form, he repeated the noun she had just given and she said صح before supplying the verb - that is still her supplying a word he did not know. He then used نراجع right at 02:50.

rows.medi_said: آآآ، الشمال الـ، روسيا the, the north of Russia. الشمال.
rows.why: Idafa: the first word never takes el-; he said el-shamaal (el-)Russia for 'the north of Russia', Amal recast شمال روسيا and repeated it at 05:37 when he said الشمال الـ روس again (one row, the first; 06:02 الشمال روس is the same moment).

rows.why: Habitual present about the north of Russia: his first بيكون (06:02) had the b-, the second (ويكون, 06:09) lost it with no modal or time word before it to drop it; Amal let it pass; low because 'وبيكون' can be misheard as 'ويكون' by the engine.
rows.english: it is very cold and it rains or snows
rows.r3_why: Only r2 saw it; the transcript shows the b- present on the first bikoon and missing on the second with nothing to license the drop, so it is a real but unproven grammar-B (she gave no signal); filed under B1 (present b-) with B8 as the ykoon context, kept low.

rows.why: The cities around him are plural but he said singular قريب; she prompted 'شو جمع قريب؟' (engine wrote غريب/غراب for قريب/قراب), he tried قريبين at 10:34, she gave the broken plural قراب and he repeated it at 10:37.

rows.why: Explaining how to build the verb from 5arbaan he said bn3eed (we repeat) for 'we add'; Amal recast bazeed (sheet: i add | Bazeed | بزيد) and he then used بزيد at 11:55; could partly be the engine hearing z as 3.
rows.r3_challenge: بنعيد vs بنزيد differ by one root letter (ع for ز) in the middle of a sound-letter drill (بـ aim الـ an); this may be an S4 root-letter slip rather than the lexical item 'repeat' for 'add' - he said بنعيد again at 11:47 after her بزيد, then بزيد at 11:55, so an audio check should decide whether he meant the wrong word or just mis-sounded it.

rows.why: Amal asked how to say 'from the end of the word'; he said ta7t (under) the word, she prompted 'The end' in English and he fixed آخر الكلمة which she confirmed (sheet: last / the end of | 2aa5er | آخر).

She asked where the b- goes ('To the beginning ... of it'); he answered bare أول الكلمة with no preposition; her reply reads as لأول الكلمة (la- 'to', engine split as لا، أول - a plain 'no' before the same words makes no sense) and he at once took it as 'لأول الـ-- في أول الكلمة', which she accepted (mm-hmm). Low because the engine's لا could still be 'no'.
rows.english: to the beginning of the word
rows.r3_why: Her line cannot be 'no' followed by the identical phrase, so it is a recast adding the preposition, and his instant لأول shows he heard it that way; a real but weak D1 row - kept at low confidence.

rows.medi_said: That means to make something stop working.
rows.amal_said: مم. It's not بخرب yet. It's بخرب.
rows.wrong: بخرب = to make something stop working
rows.right: بخرَب = I stop working / I get ruined (not بخرِّب)
rows.why: Make-X vs get-X: he glossed the plain form ba5rab as the causative 'make something stop working'; Amal said it is not ba5arreb yet, it is ba5rab (I stop working), he answered 'Okay. As in I stop working.' - a meaning slip on the form, not a produced wrong form.
rows.english: I stop working / I get ruined

rows.why: Past tense she-ending: he said خربات, she recast خربت; he asked again at 16:18 'Is it خربات or خربات؟' and she repeated خربت (same moment).
Wrong word: sa77a7t-o (I corrected it, a mistake) for 'I fixed it' (the AC) - the verb is salla7t-o; Amal recast and he repeated صلح، صلحته.

rows.amal_said: بس still هذا الفعل الثاني. ... أمم، not بخرب. بخرب that would be.
rows.why: For 'everything she uses stops working' he said the causative bi5arrbu (they ruin); Amal said that is still the second verb (ba5arreb) not ba5rab, and at 21:47 gave بس بيخرب.

rows.medi_said: They stop working. Anything she uses stops working. ... [speaking Arabic] (20:49)
rows.amal_said: So it's, it's, it's just إشي. Everything my girlfriend, my fiancée uses. So it's one thing. ... كل إشي بتستعمله بيخرب.
rows.why: Verb matches its subject: kul ishi (everything) is one thing, singular, but he put the verb in the plural (they stop working / بيخربوا); Amal said 'it's just ishi ... one thing' and gave the singular بيخرب; his 20:49 Arabic is untranscribed.

rows.medi_said: Oh, but yeah, but [speaking Arabic] and then it's becha... ... Uh, but [speaking Arabic] oh, that's right, it's she and not you. [speaking Arabic]
rows.why: For 'everything she uses' he used the you-feminine form (bitsta3mli); Amal recast بتستعمل at 20:58 and again at 21:13 and he said 'that's right, it's she and not you' at 21:19 - his own words show the person slip though the engine did not write his Arabic.

rows.medi_said: Uh, but [speaking Arabic] oh, that's right, it's she and not you. [speaking Arabic]

rows.why: Didn't-know while listening to her example سفرتنا خربت لأنه ما في تذاكر; he asked the meaning, she gave it (sheet: ticket | Tazkara | تذكرة).

rows.amal_said: عزومة is feminine or masculine؟ ... خربت.
rows.why: Verb matches its subject: 3azoome is feminine so the past verb needs -at; he said 5areb, Amal asked if 3azoome is feminine, he fixed خربت، العزومة خربت.

rows.amal_said: ما؟ ... ما it didn't come. ... ما أجا.
rows.why: The reason clause 'because X didn't come': Amal prompted 'ma?' then 'ma, it didn't come', 'ma aja', and 'kamaan marra' until it was right (31:23 ممتاز); his Arabic is untranscribed so the exact missing/wrong piece (most likely the negation ma before the past verb) cannot be quoted.

Wrong word: tannoora (skirt) for 'your dress' (fustaan); Amal said no, tannoora is skirt, he fixed فستانك and she confirmed (sheet: dress | Fus6aan | فستان; skirt | Tannoora | تنورة). His تنورك also lacks the feminine -t before -ek (A3) but she did not go there.
Preposition keeps el-: 'by accident' is bil-8ala6 (sheet: accidentally | Bil8ala6 | بالغلط); he said bi-8ala6 without el-, Amal recast بالغلط and he repeated it.
Feminine -t before the owner: jallaaye + -ek = jallaayt-ek; he said jallaay-ek, Amal prompted 'jallaaye?' and he fixed جلايتك which she confirmed (sheet: dish washer | Jallaay | جلاي).

rows.amal_said: مش، مش أزتم or it's past also.
rows.why: kaan = was: 'they didn't mean to' is past, so it needs kaan; he said mish 2asdhom (present), Amal said 'it's past also' (engine wrote مش أزتم for mish 2asdhom), he reached ما كان قصدهم at 42:45 and she said ممتاز.

rows.medi_said: Uh, مش كان and, uh, مش...
rows.amal_said: Not مش. [تضحك] If you use can. Not can.
rows.why: Saying no: ma before a verb (kaan), mish only before nouns/adjectives; he said mish kaan, Amal said 'Not mish' and he fixed ما كان قصدهم.

rows.amal_said: So، في عندنا خلاص ما can is a verb. Because can and then the verb after it should be what؟
rows.why: Verb after a verb loses its b- and is bare present: after ma kaan 2asdhom the next verb is y5arrbu, not the past 5arrabu; Amal asked what the verb after kaan should be, he answered 'present tense ... yecharbu' and she said صح.
rows.english: they didn't mean to ruin (your work)

rows.why: Noun + adjective: el-jaw shoab is a sentence (the weather is hot); as the subject 'the hot weather ruins my phone' the adjective takes el- too (el-jaw el-shoab); Amal recast الشوب and he fixed الجو الشوب بيخرب تلفوني (ممتاز).

rows.amal_said: So it's بخرررب. There is a, there is a double medal here. ... No. ... خرب.
rows.why: Commands: a doubled-middle verb takes no i- prefix in the command (5arreb, like the rule she then drilled: no 'a' when the middle is doubled or the verb is short); he said i5rab / i5rabi, Amal said no and gave خرّب, he fixed خَرِّب، خَرّبي، خَرّبوا.

rows.amal_said: Mm-mm, no. [speaks Arabic] ... So they are what's breaking. Did you break them?
rows.right: بيضلوا يخربوا (bare بيخربوا form, they break down)
rows.why: 'Why do your keys keep stopping working': Amal said no and then 'they are what's breaking' which points at him having used the causative y5arrbu (they ruin) for the plain y5rabu; her Arabic is untranscribed and the engine wrote no shadda, so the exact form is uncertain.
rows.english: why do your keys keep breaking

rows.why: Past tense: 'did you break them' is past, he said the present bit5arrbi; Amal prompted 'Did you?', he said 'Oh, past tense' and fixed إنت خربتيهم with the object ending, which she accepted.
Future with ra7 takes a bare verb: he started ra7 bit5a-, Amal said 'no b' (engine wrote نوبي), he dropped the b- and after the next fix reached راح تخربيها at 56:52.

rows.amal_said: No two T. Why two Ts؟ شوربة is feminine. So... ... one T. ... اه، راح تخربيها.
rows.why: Make-X vs get-X form: 'if you put too much salt you will ruin the soup' is ra7 t5arrbi-ha (doubled middle, one t); he built a two-t form ra7 tit5arrbi (mixing the t- get-X shape with the you-prefix), Amal said 'No two T ... one T' and he fixed راح تخربيها ('that's right').

rows.amal_said: Yes, بس we're talking about شوربة. So...
rows.why: Verb matches its subject: shoorba is feminine so 'it will go bad' is ra7 t5rab; he said ra7 y5rab, Amal reminded him the subject is shoorba, he fixed رح تخرب and she said صح.
